title: The Shackles First Appear
next_chapter_hook: The seal in the core area of the ruins is slowly crumbling, a breath surpassing Chen Ji's comprehension surging from the depths, as if something is awakening...

text.content: Deep within the mural, those eyes dormant for ten thousand years slowly opened, their pupils swirling with chaotic light, as if having traversed endless years, gazing upon everything in this realm. Chen Ji felt every hair on his body stand on end, a bone-piercing chill rushing from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head. That gaze held no malice, yet carried a suffocating scrutiny—as if he were a fish placed on the cutting board, being examined for where to begin the cut.

dialogue.content: ...You've finally seen it. Mo Xiansheng's voice resonated in his heart, ancient and weary, with a trace of undeniable sorrow: Earlier than I anticipated. Those eyes you witnessed are the lingering consciousness of the Heavenly Secrets Record's original master—or rather, the first shackle etched into the very marrow of the Heavenly Secrets Record.

text.content: The first shackle? Chen Ji's voice echoed through the empty stone chamber, hoarse and trembling. He unconsciously gripped the fragment in his hand, his knuckles white from the pressure. Mo Xiansheng had told him that the Heavenly Secrets Record was a heaven-defying object, and every volume came with a price. But he never imagined that this price was inscribed from the very beginning upon the artifact itself—an invisible shackle placed around the neck of every inheritor.

dialogue.content: The mural is changing. Those ancient lines began to flow, rippling like water before ultimately converging into a clear image: seven fragments scattered across heaven and earth, each enveloped by seven different lights. And at the very center, a human figure was bound by countless chains, every chain connected to one fragment. Mo Xiansheng's voice turned bitter: Only by collecting all seven pages can the shackles be released. But the more pages you hold, the deeper your karma with heaven becomes... until in the end, there is no path left to retreat.

text.content: Chen Ji stared at the image in the mural, his chest feeling as if gripped by an iron hand, the pain almost making it impossible to breathe. He recalled all his calculations along the way—using the Heavenly Secrets Record to foresee the future, consuming his Heavenly Fate Value for intelligence advantages, navigating the machinations of the three great sects. He thought he was using this heaven-defying artifact, yet he never realized that from the very beginning, he was the one being used. Heaven granted him the ability to foresee destiny, but had already marked the price in the shadows.

So that's how it is. So I never had any choice in the first place. He murmured to himself, his voice terrifyingly hollow. Every use of the Heavenly Secrets Record was reinforcing those shackles; every glimpse of the future was embedding himself deeper into this chess game. He suddenly understood the fates of all those seers throughout history—they didn't die from heavenly retribution, but from their own choices. Every glimpse of heavenly secrets was depleting the roots of their lives, until one day, those roots collapsed and everything turned to dust.

Footsteps echoed from the other end of the stone chamber. Chen Ji didn't turn around—he knew who had arrived. In the depths of these ruins, the only one who could accompany him was Su Qingyao. That cold and proud Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, that woman who had come infinitely close to the truth three times yet had been skillfully deflected by him each time. Why was she here now, when she should have stayed at the sect? A flicker of vigilance crossed Chen Ji's heart, but more than that was an unspeakable exhaustion.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji! Su Qingyao's voice carried suppressed urgency. She strode quickly to his side, her gaze sweeping over the mural, her pupils contracting sharply. What is this... Her voice trembled slightly, but she didn't press further, instead turning to Chen Ji's pale face, a flicker of heartache in her eyes. How long have you been standing here? Your complexion... What exactly did you see?

text.content: Chen Ji offered no answer. He simply stood there quietly, his gaze still fixed on the figure bound by chains in the mural. The figure's face was unclear, but the outline... the outline bore a striking resemblance to himself. Seven fragments, seven shackles. A sudden urge to laugh seized him—he had gone to great lengths to collect the fragments, believing he was strengthening his abilities and positioning himself in the world, never knowing that each fragment collected was merely adding another layer of new shackles upon himself.

dialogue.content: You're thinking about giving up, aren't you? Su Qingyao's voice suddenly turned cold, carrying a sharpness Chen Ji had never heard before. She seized his collar, forcing him to meet her gaze: You think I can't see it? From the moment you entered these ruins, your eyes have been wrong. What are you thinking? Thinking that the Heavenly Secrets Record is a curse, that you should throw it away? Chen Ji, what do you take me for? Do you have any idea how worried I've been, rushing here alone?

text.content: Su Qingyao's eyes were slightly reddened, yet she stubbornly refused to let tears fall. She was the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, the pride of the Tianqing Sect, always the one coldly observing the mortal world, never moved by anyone. But thistrash杂役, this man she had been investigating for three years yet never fully understood, had unknowingly entered the softest corner of her heart. Now he stood here, his face written with resignation, filling her with an aching fear.

dialogue.content: Do you know what I hate most? Su Qingyao's voice dropped, trembling with a sob: What I hate most is that composed look of yours. No matter what happens, you always have that expression—as if you've calculated everything, as if nothing concerns you. But have you ever thought, in every step you've calculated, whether you factored in our safety? Whether you factored in... me?

text.content: Chen Ji finally reacted. He lowered his head, looking at Su Qingyao's hand gripping his collar, that hand trembling slightly from the force. He suddenly recalled everything over these three years—every time he used the Heavenly Secrets Record and consumed his Heavenly Fate Value, she would mysteriously send him various "coincidental" supplies afterward; every time he fell into danger, she would conveniently appear nearby. She wasn't oblivious, but had chosen to protect him despite knowing. This foolish woman...

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao's interrogation was like a blade piercing through Chen Ji's defenses. Looking at her reddened eyes, a crack appeared in the ice wall of his heart. How should he respond to this woman who had been secretly protecting him for three years?

choices.description: Drop all pretense and calculations, tell Su Qingyao the truth about the Heavenly Secrets Record's shackles, as well as his inner fears and struggles.
choices.visible_reward: Establish a deeper bond with Su Qingyao, unlock the prerequisite conditions for the 「Shared Destiny」 buff
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao may be drawn into deeper heavenly karma as a result

text.content: Chen Ji reached out, gently covering Su Qingyao's trembling hand with his own. She froze but didn't pull away. He could feel the coldness of her fingertips and the slightly accelerated pulse beneath them. ...You're right. I never factored anyone into my calculations. He gave a bitter smile: Because I thought I had no right to make anyone worry. The price of the Heavenly Secrets Record... is more terrible than you could imagine.

choices.memory_label: 陈机在苏青瑶面前展露脆弱

choices.description: Use the usualtrash persona to hide the inner turmoil, tell Su Qingyao he was merely contemplating life, that he's not worth her worry.
choices.visible_cost: Su Qingyao may develop greater suspicion
choices.visible_reward: Maintain the persona, retain trump cards

text.content: Chen Ji gently released Su Qingyao's hand, a faint smile curling at his lips—a smile so gentle it sent a chill through the heart: Sister Su, you're overthinking. I was merely contemplating how interesting the patterns in this mural are... If Sister Su is interested, shall we contemplate it together? His voice was calm as ever, but his eyes deliberately avoided Su Qingyao's gaze.

choices.description: Don't answer her questions directly, instead ask Su Qingyao why she came to the depths of the ruins, implying danger may be approaching.
choices.visible_cost: May miss the opportunity for honesty
choices.visible_reward: Obtain key intelligence, protect Su Qingyao's safety
choices.risk_hint: The topic change may make Su Qingyao even more displeased

text.content: Chen Ji didn't answer her interrogation. Instead, he slightly frowned: Sister Su, how did you enter these ruins? The outer seal here requires at least Nascent Soul cultivation to break, yet you and I... His gaze turned sharp: Did you use some forbidden technique? Why is your aura so chaotic?

Just then, a low rumble echoed from the depths of the stone chamber. The images on the mural shifted once more—the positions of the seven fragments began to flicker, as if pointing toward something. Chen Ji's heart stirred—that was the resonance between the fragments. He had collected three pages already; if the mural was true, then the remaining four pages... Just as he contemplated, a blinding golden light erupted from the end of the stone chamber, illuminating the entire space.

The seal in the ruins' core area... is crumbling! Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly rang out, carrying unprecedented solemnity: Chen Ji, that is what lies deepest within these ruins—not fragments, but the final legacy left by the original master of the Heavenly Secrets Record. Someone... someone triggered the mechanism before us. Quickly! If you want to obtain the fourth page, you must reach the core before them!

choice.prompt: The ruins' core is about to open, but the truth of the shackles still looms like dark clouds. Chen Ji must make a choice—continue pursuing the fragments or find another way to break free from destiny?

choices.description: Accept the shackles of destiny and continue pursuing the fragments. Though the shackles exist, as long as all seven are not collected, there is still room for maneuver.
choices.visible_cost: The shackles deepen, and the karma with heaven becomes harder to sever
choices.visible_reward: Obtain clues to the fourth fragment; the ruins' core may hold greater opportunities
choices.risk_hint: The appearance of unknown competitors increases variables

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, turned to look at Su Qingyao. His eyes were no longer hollow as before, but rekindled with familiar sharpness and depth. ...Sister Su, are you willing to walk this path with me? He extended his hand, his tone calm yet carrying unyielding resolve: Since destiny wishes to shackle me, then I shall grasp these shackles in my hand and wield them as weapons.

choices.description: Stop pursuing the fragments and seek other methods to break free from the shackles. Perhaps if the seven pages are not all collected, the shackles won't fully lock in place.
choices.visible_cost: Lose the opportunity for rapid strength improvement
choices.visible_reward: Temporarily preserve Heavenly Fate Value, avoid deeper heavenly karma
choices.risk_hint: May miss key clues to unlocking the shackles

text.content: Chen Ji shook his head, his gaze falling on the figure bound by chains in the mural. ...Since collecting all seven pages is the beginning of deepening shackles, then by not collecting them all, can I avoid that? He turned to Su Qingyao: Sister, help me search the records of all past Heavenly Secrets Record inheritors. Perhaps... perhaps there is another path. His tone unusually carried a plea.

Su Qingyao looked at the hand Chen Ji had extended, her heart filled with countless emotions. She knew this man never easily asked others for help, never displayed weakness before others. That moment of candor just now was something precious she had never witnessed in three years. And now, watching his fighting spirit rekindle, she felt a heartaching relief. ...Alright. She didn't hesitate, reaching out to grasp his hand: Whatever you choose, I will walk this path with you.

The moment their hands touched, those eyes in the mural flickered. A subtle piece of information flowed into Chen Ji's mind—something Mo Xiansheng had never mentioned: The fourth fragment lies in the deepest part of the ruins' core, and guarding it... is a trial that only those holding one or more fragments can pass. Chen Ji's pupils contracted, his heart skipping a beat. He didn't know what this trial meant, but intuition told him the path ahead would by no means be smooth.

The golden light at the end of the stone chamber grew brighter, an ancient and mysterious aura filling the air. Chen Ji released Su Qingyao's hand, turned to face the core area about to open. His back remained slender, his steps still composed, but only he knew that at this moment, his heart was churning like a raging sea. The shackles have appeared, but the key to unlocking them has also revealed itself. He could not retreat, would not retreat. Because behind him stood those he must protect; within his heart lay the truth he must pursue. The core area of the ruins slowly opens, and those mysterious eyes that had been watching everything quietly close within the mural's depths—as if waiting, waiting for this chess game to move toward its final conclusion.
